wire.runtime_memory.approval_stop_local_: force-stop {address}: signals it even while it is working (SIGTERM, a bounded drain, then SIGKILL), so work in flight is cut
wire.runtime_memory.enabled.help: End a session runtime whose own memory stays over the ceiling below for several consecutive checks (about three minutes). Its wakes and monitors are made dormant, not deleted, and the session is told why when it next opens.
wire.runtime_memory.enabled.label: Session memory limit
wire.runtime_memory.limit_mb.help: How much memory one session runtime may hold before the guard ends it. The default sits well above the largest session measured in normal use; values below 1024 are raised to 1024, and 0 means the default.
wire.runtime_memory.limit_mb.label: Session ceiling (MB)
wire.runtime_memory.section.description: A ceiling on each session runtime's own memory, so one runaway session is ended instead of pushing the whole device into swap.
wire.runtime_memory.section.title: Session memory limit
wire.runtime_memory.stop_force_hint: If the operator asked for this session to be ended, or it is a memory runaway, call stop again with force=true: that sends an identity-checked SIGTERM, waits out its bounded drain, then sends SIGKILL to that exact process, and the work in flight is cut. Otherwise this refusal is the answer.
